title: Dark Mediterranean
meta_description: Dark Mediterranean is an in-progress hospitality image study for a real estate agency: a 3D massing model of a hypothetical resort, turned into a sequence of blue-hour frames that all agree with it.
deck: An in-progress hospitality study for a real estate agency, where the resort is hypothetical but its geometry is not: the building is modelled first, and every generated frame has to agree with the model it came from.

proof.title: The same building in every frame.
proof.note: The set is generated from one 3D massing model, so the roofline, the step of the terraces and the position of the pool are settled before a prompt is written. Distance and light are free to move. Geometry is not, because an agency is selling something that has to be buildable.

shots.alt: Dusk view through dark foliage of a stepped blue lime-washed resort building on a forested hillside, one warm-lit doorway reflected in a narrow lap pool.
shots.caption: Camera 01 / the approach, from outside the boundary

shots.alt: Blue corridor of receding portals framing a candlelit lounge with white cushions, terracotta vessels and a low carved table at the far end.
shots.caption: Camera 05 / the entrance corridor, held on axis

shots.alt: Three-by-three grid of blue-hour resort frames moving from the hillside approach and pool terrace to lit windows, a laid dinner table and a single lantern.
shots.caption: Curated grid / nine camera positions, in order of approach

shots.alt: Alternate three-by-three grid of the same blue resort with sea-facing terraces, a table set against a blank wall, and a parasol standing in still water.
shots.caption: Superset / positions that broke continuity and were cut

proof.caption: A frame that flatters the site but moves a wall is worth nothing to an agency, so every image here traces back to a camera position on the model. The set is meant to be read as a document of one building, not as a mood board about blue.

acts.title: Establishing to intimate.
acts.note: The nine positions are set on the model as a walk a buyer could actually take, which is also the order an agency needs: the site first, then the building, then the room being sold.

items.title: The hillside
items.copy: The resort seen whole, through trees, from outside its own boundary. The row that has to prove the site.

items.title: The threshold
items.copy: Windows and doorways, each one a lit interior read from the cold side of the wall. The row where the elevations have to hold.

items.title: The table
items.copy: Dinner laid, loungers turned out, a lantern left on. Occupied, and empty. The row that sells the room.

pipeline.title: Pipeline.
pipeline.note: Built as a Runway workflow so the model does the deciding. The massing render conditions every generation, which leaves the prompt responsible for light and mood and nothing structural.

items.label: Model
items.copy: The resort built as 3D massing first, with site, levels and sightlines resolved before any frame exists.

items.label: Position
items.copy: Camera positions set on the model and numbered, so each final frame has a coordinate rather than a description.

items.label: Condition
items.copy: Each position rendered out and passed into the workflow as the reference the generation has to agree with.

items.label: Verify
items.copy: Frames read back against the model and cut when a wall, a level or a sightline has moved.

items.label: Grade
items.copy: Warm interiors protected so they survive as the single accent against the blue.
